Bug_Title: Eq: equals method compares class names rather than class objects (EQ_COMPARING_CLASS_NAMES)
Bug_Details:
This class defines an equals method that checks to see if two objects are the same class by checking to see if the names
of their classes are equal. You can have different classes with the same name if they are loaded by
different class loaders. Just check to see if the class objects are the same.
Bug_Explanation: The equals method in the main method checks if two objects are the same class by comparing their class names, rather than checking if the class objects are the same. This bug can be triggered by using different class loaders to load different classes with the same name.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggered the bug by creating two objects with the same class name, but different class objects. The equals method compared the class names of the objects, resulting in a false positive.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the equals method is comparing class names rather than class objects, which is a violation of the bug rule. Specifically, the test code creates two objects of type Object and checks if they are equal using the equals method. The test code then asserts that the result of the equals method is false, which is correct because the two objects are not the same class, even though they have the same class name. This confirms that the bug is triggered in the provided Java code.
